memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At that time I commanded Joshua: "You have seen with your own eyes all that the Lord your God has done to these two kings. The Lord will do the same to all the kingdoms over there where you are going. Do not be afraid of them; the Lord your God himself will fight for you." - Deut 3:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses now turns to Joshua, who would lead Israel after him, and gives him a word of encouragement grounded in what God had already done: "You have seen with your own eyes all that the Lord your God has done to these two kings." The victories over Sihon and Og were not just history; they were evidence for the future. Because God had defeated these kings, Joshua could trust Him to defeat the kingdoms ahead. "Do not be afraid... the Lord your God himself will fight for you."

This is such a wise way to build courage. Moses did not tell Joshua to summon confidence from within himself or to rely on his own abilities. He pointed him to God's proven track record. Faith for the future is fueled by memory of the past. What God has done becomes the ground for trusting what God will do.

We can encourage ourselves and others in the same way. When facing new fears, we look back at how God has already helped us. Has He provided before? Then He can provide again. Has He made a way before? Then He can make a way again. The God who fought for us yesterday is the same God who goes before us tomorrow.

And notice the heart of the promise: "the Lord your God himself will fight for you." The battle does not ultimately rest on us. God Himself fights for His people. This was true for Joshua, and it is gloriously true for us in Christ. On the cross, God fought and won our greatest battle, and He continues to work on our behalf. If God is for us, who can be against us (Rom 8:31)? Draw courage from His past faithfulness, and go forward trusting the God who fights for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How can you draw courage from God's past faithfulness for a present fear?
2. Who might you encourage by reminding them of what God has done?
3. What does it mean to you that "the Lord Himself will fight for you"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that You have proven Yourself faithful again and again. When new fears arise, help me remember Your past victories and go forward trusting that You Yourself will fight for me, as You did supremely at the cross. Amen.
